literature_notes: The sole ledger line (L1) reports mouse ITGA6 cloned into the CD63-pEGFP C2 vector backbone (Addgene #62964) using SacI and EcoRI restriction sites. Addgene #62964 is a construct in which EGFP is fused to the intracellular C-terminus of CD63 (a tetraspanin whose C-terminus faces the cytoplasm). When ITGA6 replaces CD63 in this backbone, EGFP is placed at the intracellular C-terminus of ITGA6 (residue 1130, topology INTRACELLULAR per landmarks). The alternative reading — EGFP N-terminal to ITGA6 — would place EGFP upstream of the signal peptide (residues 1–23), where it would be co-translationally cleaved or cause misfolding; this is not a valid extracellular surface tag. In neither reading does L1 support an extracellular surface tag. Additionally, the ledger clip does not state the junction residue, so the commercial-plasmid exclusion ('a commercial plasmid whose tag position is unstated; you cannot pin insert_after_residue') independently bars it from sites. No other ledger lines exist. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: Mouse ITGA6 fused to EGFP via the CD63-pEGFP C2 backbone (Addgene #62964); the vector places EGFP at the intracellular C-terminus of the insert protein, corresponding to residue 1130 of ITGA6, which lies in the cytoplasmic tail (topology INTRACELLULAR, residues 1077–1130).
